items.headline: Jalen Duren Skips Pistons Media Day Amid Contract Dispute
items.summary: DET restricted free agent C Jalen Duren is expected to miss the Pistons' Media Day and the start of training camp due to an ongoing contract standoff. Duren reportedly rejected a five-year, $200M offer and is seeking a max deal, facing a Thursday deadline to accept his qualifying offer.

items.headline: Warriors' Kristaps Porzingis Out Indefinitely with Health Issue
items.summary: GSW big man Kristaps Porzingis is sidelined indefinitely as training camp opens due to a recurring health issue, postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome (POTS). Porzingis appeared in only 32 games last season for the Warriors after being acquired from the ATL.

items.headline: Lakers Acquire Walker Kessler from Jazz in Sign-and-Trade
items.summary: The LAL have completed a sign-and-trade deal to acquire C Walker Kessler from the UTA Jazz. The Lakers sent two unprotected first-round picks and two first-round pick swaps to the Jazz, while Kessler signed a four-year, $130M contract with Los Angeles.

items.headline: Bulls Trade for Buddy Hield from Hornets
items.summary: The CHI Bulls have acquired veteran guard Buddy Hield and cash from the CHA Hornets in exchange for guard Rob Dillingham. This marks Hield's second trade in five days, having previously been moved from ATL to Charlotte.

items.headline: Clippers, Heat Make Late Offseason Signings
items.summary: The LAC have signed Blake Wesley to a one-year contract, adding depth to their backcourt. Meanwhile, the MIA Heat have brought in free agent guard Dennis Smith Jr. on a deal.

items.headline: Spurs Embrace Heightened Expectations as Western Conference Champions
items.summary: The SAS entered their Media Day with elevated expectations after capturing the NBA Western Conference championship last season, focusing on continued improvement.

items.headline: Offseason Sees Significant Coaching Turnover Across NBA
items.summary: The 2026 offseason has seen a widespread coaching carousel, with several franchises, including CHI (Tiago Splitter), DAL (Dusty May), MIL (Taylor Jenkins), NOP (Jamahl Mosley), ORL (Sean Sweeney), POR (Micah Nori), and WAS (Brian Keefe), reshaping their leadership ahead of the 2026-27 season.
